alt: Gray, rough lunar rock on a white table with a small cube labeled W and a ruler
title: Gray Lunar Rock
text: A rough gray rock brought back from the Moon. The ID number on the label lets scientists track every sample in the lab. The small cube and ruler are used to show size and color.

alt: Black and white photo of a dark lunar rock inside a sealed laboratory chamber, image mirrored
title: Rock in the Sample Lab
text: Lunar rocks were studied inside sealed chambers so Moon material would not be contaminated by Earth air. This photo is mirrored, which is why the label looks reversed.

alt: Black and white photo of bootprints and a flag on the lunar surface next to a landing module leg
title: Footprints in the Regolith
text: The Moon has no wind or rain, so footprints in the dust can last for a very long time. Walking here taught engineers how lunar soil behaves under boots and wheels.

alt: Black and white photo of a pile of fine dark lunar soil on a white surface
title: Lunar Soil (Regolith)
text: Regolith is the loose, powdery dust and broken rock that covers the Moon. It is sharp and sticky, so it can wear down suits and clog equipment. Habitats and rovers must be designed to handle it.

alt: Small rounded lunar rock next to a ruler and a cube labeled Si, with the number 10026,10
title: Small Lunar Rock
text: A small rock photographed beside a millimeter ruler and a color cube so its size can be measured. Even a rock this small can tell scientists about the Moon's history.
